summary: Latency regression on INT8 model variant after runtime update (p95 TPOT up ~35%); workaround needed (pin/rollback)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports a latency regression after the 2025-10-14 runtime update on their Dedicated cluster. Regression appears limited to INT8 variants (FP16 path appears unchanged).

Customer impact
- Production traffic for chat workloads. Customer reports user-visible slow responses and timeouts in downstream UI.
- Symptoms: higher TPOT (time-per-output-token) and occasional queueing spikes under moderate concurrency.

Observed deltas (customer-provided + Redwood spot-check)
- Before update (runtime build ~2025-10-08): p95 TPOT ~33–38 ms/token, p95 TTFT ~0.7–0.9s at concurrency=32.
- After update (runtime build ~2025-10-14): p95 TPOT ~46–55 ms/token (+25–45%), p95 TTFT ~0.8–1.1s (small increase).
- Regression is more pronounced on long decode (>= 256 output tokens). Prefill phase looks similar.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: heliocrm-dedicated-03
- Region: us-east
- GPU: H100 80GB (customer states), no MIG
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (streaming=true)
- Models affected: llama-3.1-70b-instruct-int8, qwen2.5-72b-instruct-int8

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Use the customer’s same decoding params: temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, max_tokens=512, stream=true.
2) Concurrency 32, mixed prompt lengths (128–2k tokens).
3) Compare runtime build 2025-10-08 vs 2025-10-14.

Initial hypotheses
- INT8 kernel auto-selector choosing a suboptimal kernel for specific shapes after the update (decode-heavy shapes likely), or falling back to FP16 kernel for certain INT8 shapes.
- Scheduler changes interacting with INT8 decode (batch-size cap / interleaving) causing worse tail under mixed prompt lengths.

Logs / references
- Customer sample request IDs: rwd_req_8f3c1a7b, rwd_req_91b6e2d0 (approx 2025-10-15 09:10–09:25 PT)
- Redwood internal dashboard link: (see Support private note in comments; contains customer identifiers)

Requested outcome
- Provide immediate mitigation (pin/rollback/flag) while Engineering investigates.
- Confirm whether a known issue exists and whether a hotfix is available.
comments: 2025-10-15 10:02 PT — Aisha Bello (Support) — Acknowledged. Asked customer for: exact runtime version/build ID, GPU type/MIG, concurrency and prompt distribution, and 2–3 request IDs spanning before/after. Confirmed we can provide a rollback/pin as mitigation if regression confirmed.

2025-10-15 10:24 PT — Customer (HelioCRM) — Provided details: runtime was updated during scheduled maintenance window to build tag rwd-runtime-2025.10.14.2. GPUs are H100 80GB, no MIG. Regression only when using *-int8 variants. FP16 versions stable. Attached screenshots of their p95 rising ~40% on decode-heavy endpoints. Provided request IDs and timestamps.

2025-10-15 11:05 PT — Noah Patel (Runtime Perf) — Confirmed we’ve seen similar behavior in lab for a subset of INT8 decode shapes post-2025.10.14, likely kernel selection/fallback. Looping in Yuki Sato (auto-selection) + Marcus Reed (scheduler) for quick triage. Immediate workaround: pin runtime back to 2025.10.08 or disable INT8 path via runtime config while we validate a fix.

2025-10-15 11:18 PT — Aisha Bello (Support) — Shared mitigation options with customer:
1) Roll back runtime to rwd-runtime-2025.10.08.x (recommended).
2) Alternatively pin affected routes to FP16 variants temporarily.
3) If rollback not possible today, we can apply a config override to force legacy INT8 kernel family (may trade throughput for stability).
Asked customer to confirm preferred option and whether they can tolerate a brief maintenance restart.

2025-10-15 13:42 PT — Customer (HelioCRM) — Requested rollback to prior build. FP16 pinning is acceptable as a fallback but they prefer INT8 for cost. Approved maintenance restart today after 18:00 PT.

2025-10-15 18:36 PT — Sean Gallagher (SRE) — Rolled cluster heliocrm-dedicated-03 back to rwd-runtime-2025.10.08.4. Restart completed. Monitoring for 30 minutes. Early signals show TPOT back in expected range. Noted: leaving a temporary dashboard annotation for the rollback window.

2025-10-15 19:22 PT — Aisha Bello (Support) — Confirmed with customer: metrics recovered post-rollback. Customer confirms UI responsiveness is back to baseline. Keeping ticket open pending Engineering root cause and forward fix guidance so they can safely upgrade again.

2025-10-16 09:10 PT — Noah Patel (Runtime Perf) — Root cause likely: auto-selector bug choosing FP16 kernel for a subset of INT8 shapes (decode) after recent refactor; fix in review (see PR 10625). Also evaluating scheduler batch-size cap change interaction, but primary regression signature matches kernel mismatch. We’ll recommend customer stays pinned until fix is released and validated in perf-canary.

2025-10-17 14:55 PT — Aisha Bello (Support) — Update to customer: fix is in progress and being validated with quant-perf canary. We will provide a target maintenance build once canary passes. Customer requested release notes / upgrade steps when available.

2025-10-18 11:30 PT — Aisha Bello (Support) — Ticket resolved with rollback mitigation. Follow-up action: notify customer when patched runtime build containing INT8 selector fix is available and provide recommended config for safe rollout (canary + quick rollback).
resolution: Mitigated by rolling back Dedicated cluster heliocrm-dedicated-03 from rwd-runtime-2025.10.14.2 to rwd-runtime-2025.10.08.4. Latency (TPOT) returned to baseline. Engineering investigating forward fix; suspected INT8 kernel auto-selection mismatch for certain decode shapes. Customer advised to remain pinned or temporarily route to FP16 until patched build is validated.
next_steps: Engineering: land and validate fix for INT8 kernel auto-selection mismatch; verify against decode-heavy workloads and mixed prompt distributions.
SRE/Support: when patched build is available, coordinate a canary upgrade window with HelioCRM and provide a rollback plan.
Perf/Observability: add a targeted quant-perf canary scenario that matches customer workload shape (streaming, concurrency=32, long decode) to prevent recurrence.
